scenes.say: Why should software engineers care about bundle size? Does it really matter for web performance?

scenes.label: Bundle
scenes.sub: All JavaScript sent to the browser.
scenes.say: Bundle size is the total amount of JavaScript your site sends to the browser. The bigger it is, the slower your site loads.
Tree shaking removes unused code. The bundler analyzes your imports, deletes dead exports, and keeps only what's actually used.
Code splitting breaks your code into smaller chunks. With Webpack, you can use dynamic import to load code only when it's needed.

scenes.question: How do you check your bundle size?
scenes.wrong: Just look at the file list.
scenes.right: Use tools like Webpack Bundle Analyzer to visualize and optimize your bundle.
scenes.say: Interview trap: How do you check your bundle size? Don't just eyeball the file list. Use tools like Webpack Bundle Analyzer to really understand what's inside.
